title: Introducing NSE Day Trader Skills – an open-source AI toolkit built for the Indian stock market
author: Strange-Tomorrow-174
selftext:
I've been working on something interesting: giving AI agents the ability to understand and analyse the Indian NSE market using specialised skills.  
Instead of building another trading indicator, I created a collection of 13 specialised AI agent skills covering:  
📊 NSE Market Scanning  
📈 FII/DII Activity Analysis  
📰 Market News Analysis  
🎯 Entry & Exit Planning  
⏳ Historical Market Simulation  
💰 Position Sizing & Budget Management  
🛡️ Risk Management  
📋 Manual Broker Order Tickets  
**What makes it different?**  
Designed around Indian NSE conventions.  
Compatible with Claude Code, OpenCode and other compatible AI agents.  
Python-based standalone CLI tools.  
No paid API required.  
Broker-neutral, with no automatic order execution.  
Open-source under the MIT licence.  
My goal is to make AI-powered market analysis more accessible to Indian developers and traders.  
GitHub: [**https://lnkd.in/grsp-ZNM**](https://www.linkedin.com/safety/go/?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2Fgrsp-ZNM&urlhash=iNK4&mt=qFcYHwL_yQ9GzX0QUsylnKZzpEfFi4r7SfQYQQOo_crffTXJfrlCU3Xdx4TIQcK8YjchpJ0fh1m63cX421-hunH7EoOHlnVPdOC4_WSTW7JArV8NXToC91UyLW5s3b7en9xSG7pK1d0bg--hZCtkVvEJv-Owc5hTCZHaxINvH9Ka16_As5W1FhfUbDtmv_lt_Go&isSdui=true)  
I'd love to hear feedback from AI developers, algo traders and the Indian trading community.  
If you're interested, give it a try and let me know what you think!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: stopping at a manual order ticket instead of wiring it straight to the broker is a sensible line for v1. FII/DII numbers come out after the close though, so I'd keep that skill away from intraday entry calls.

replies.author: Strange-Tomorrow-174
replies.body:
Thanks, really appreciate the feedback!

Yeah, the manual order ticket was intentional for V1. I wanted to keep the final order placement in the user's hands instead of wiring an AI agent directly to a broker API.

And you're absolutely right about the FII/DII timing. The project already has some data-date alignment and warning logic, but I agree the rule should be much more explicit. FII/DII data should be treated as previous-session/end-of-day context, not as live same-day institutional flow or a direct intraday entry trigger.

I'm going to tighten that up by clearly showing the data date/session and making sure it can't be misinterpreted as a real-time intraday signal.

Really useful point — this is exactly the kind of feedback I was hoping to get. Thanks again!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the date right next to the number should cover it. I hit the same thing building Quantradin (quantradin.com, paper trading only): anything published after the close looked live until it carried its own session date.

replies.author: Strange-Tomorrow-174
replies.body:
Yeah, that makes sense — putting the session date right next to the actual FII/DII numbers is probably the clearest way to handle it.

Something like `FII Net Flow — Session: 31 Oct 2026` should make it much harder to mistake end-of-day data for live intraday data.

Interesting that you ran into the same issue with Quantradin too. I'll definitely make the session date more prominent in the output. Thanks again for sharing your experience!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: yeah, the label does most of the work. the case that caught me after that was Mondays and holidays, where the last session is two or three days back and still reads as fresh unless something flags the gap.

replies.author: Strange-Tomorrow-174
replies.body:
Oh, that's a really good catch. I hadn't considered the Monday/holiday edge case properly.

You're right — just attaching the session date doesn't tell us whether the data is actually up to date. I'm going to add a trading-session freshness check using the NSE calendar, so Friday's data on Monday isn't incorrectly flagged as stale, but missing a newer trading session is detected.

Appreciate you sharing your experience with Quantradin. This is exactly the kind of real-world edge case I want to catch before expanding the project further!
